items.title: For perfect maps between locally Noetherian schemes, being lci is the tor-amplitude [-1,0] condition on the cotangent complex
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a perfect morphism f : X -> Y of locally Noetherian schemes the lemma gives the three-way equivalence: f is a local complete intersection morphism; NL_{X/Y} has tor-amplitude in [-1, 0]; NL_{X/Y} is perfect with tor-amplitude in [-1, 0]. The retained proof is written as the affines-to-schemes translation protocol: the chapter's lci-affine dictionary (lemma affine-lci) identifies lci-ness with the finite tor dimension condition on the naive cotangent complex of a polynomial presentation; the identification NL_{X/Y} with that naive complex on affines (chapter lemma NL-affine); the Derived Categories of Schemes comparison trio (affine-compare-bounded, tor-dimension-affine, perfect-affine) turns the module-theoretic amplitude statements into the scheme-global ones; and the resulting ring-level theorem is Divided Power Algebra, lemma perfect-NL-lci (a perfect map is lci iff its naive cotangent complex has tor-amplitude in [-1,0]). Every input is a named bridge. Retained author proof at lines 18488-18498.
